output.normalized_title: analytics-pipeline: S3 multipart upload rejected with QuotaExceeded (analytics-pipeline)
symptoms: S3 multipart upload rejected with QuotaExceeded

output.classification_reasoning: The failure is triggered by an S3 multipart upload being rejected with a QuotaExceeded error, which directly indicates that the storage quota for the analytics-pipeline's S3 bucket has been exhausted. This is a classic storage exhaustion scenario rather than a network, application, authentication, or database issue. The impact spans 3,500 users and caused a 35‑minute outage, suggesting the problem is not trivial but also not deeply entangled across multiple services. The root cause is confined to storage quota limits, requiring quota increase or cleanup, and the remediation steps are straightforward (e.g., request higher quota, delete unused objects). Therefore the incident is categorized as storage_exhaustion with a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: analytics-pipeline: S3 multipart upload rejected with QuotaExceeded

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Historical correlation indicates recurring pattern in analytics-pipeline.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
output.justification: The incident impacts 3,500 users, exceeding the cross‑tier threshold of 2,000 users defined in the SLA rule. Although the affected service is Tier‑3, the rule applies across tiers when the user count surpasses 2,000. The outage duration of 35 minutes is within typical response windows for SEV‑2 incidents, and the root cause has been confirmed with high confidence (0.95). Therefore, the deterministic rule correctly recommends SEV‑2.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Confirm the operator has root access or the ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us‑east‑1.
verification: AWS identity matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context equals prod-us-east-1

remediation_steps.title: Enforce Write‑Freeze and Promote Read‑Replica
remediation_steps.description: Coordinate with the application team to pause any new write traffic to the analytics pipeline, then promote the healthy read‑replica to become the primary storage target.
commands: # Notify downstream services to pause writes (manual step)
verification: RDS status shows 'promoting' then 'available' for the new primary
Write‑freeze acknowledgment logged in the change‑management system

remediation_steps.title: Free Up S3 Storage Quota
remediation_steps.description: Identify and delete stale multipart upload parts and old analytics artifacts that exceed retention policy to relieve storage exhaustion.
commands: aws s3api list-multipart-uploads --bucket analytics-pipeline-bucket --query 'Uploads[?Initiated<`date -d "30 days ago" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S`].UploadId' --output text > /tmp/old_uploads.txt
while read uploadId; do aws s3api abort-multipart-upload --bucket analytics-pipeline-bucket --key <object-key> --upload-id $uploadId; done < /tmp/old_uploads.txt
verification: S3 bucket metrics show storage usage < 80% of quota
No multipart uploads older than 30 days remain

remediation_steps.title: Execute Graceful Rolling Restart of Analytics Pipeline
remediation_steps.description: Trigger a rolling restart of the deployment so pods pick up the newly promoted primary and cleared storage space.
verification: All pods reach READY=1/1 and status Running
Pod logs no longer contain ERR_STORAGE_EXHAUSTION_241

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks and verify that error rates have returned to baseline.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=analytics-pipeline --since=5m | grep ERR_STORAGE_EXHAUSTION_241 || echo 'No errors'

aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/S3 --metric-name BucketSizeBytes --dimensions Name=BucketName,Value=analytics-pipeline-bucket --statistics Average --period 300 --start-time $(date -u -d '-10 minutes' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body 'OK'
Error grep returns no matches
S3 bucket size metric stable and below quota threshold

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert the deployment to the previous container image, demote the promoted replica back to read‑only, and restore any deleted S3 objects from backup if needed.

steps.description: Undo the rolling restart by rolling back to the prior image tag.
verification: Deployment revision shows previous version
Pods restart with the prior image

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica to read‑only and re‑attach the original primary (if still functional).
verification: RDS instance status returns to 'available' and role = 'read-replica'

steps.description: Restore any critical S3 objects removed during cleanup from backup snapshots.
commands: aws s3 cp s3://analytics-pipeline-backup/snapshot-$(date -u -d '1 day ago' +%Y-%m-%d).tar.gz s3://analytics-pipeline-bucket/ --recursive
verification: Restored objects appear in bucket listing
Checksum validation passes

verification_checkpoints: All rollback commands complete without error
Service health endpoint returns to pre‑remediation error state (expected for rollback)
Monitoring dashboards show original error spike re‑appears, confirming rollback effectiveness

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified (root or ProdOperations SSO)
Write‑freeze documented and approved in change‑management system
Current deployment image tag recorded for rollback
S3 backup snapshot verified and accessible
safety_verification.notes: All steps are idempotent where possible and include explicit verification before proceeding to the next step. No irreversible changes are performed without a documented rollback path.
